pr_body:
`MockSinglePrioritizingExecutor` contains a hack that stops working with
JDK19 which introduces a different way to start threads. This commit
removes the hack and captures the tasks to be executed as they're passed
to the executor instead.

It turns out this hack was also apparently swallowing some tripping
assertions, so this commit fixes those assertions.

Closes #86880

comments:
The issue seems to be that JDK19 adds a new way to start a thread, `Thread#start(ThreadContainer)` which means that it no longer works to capture and enqueue a task as done here:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/da6c79ef195df73994d84a3c9c086ef8bfdccf65/test/framework/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/MockSinglePrioritizingExecutor.java#L34-L55

review_comments: I would prefer to just have an explicit log context string passed in or an explicit wrapper, seems that would be less surprising if we ever use the wrapper for anything but adding the log context.

I know what you mean but we use a non-log-context-related wrapper in the tests - it would be a bit of a pain to assert that we wrap things correctly otherwise especially given the ongoing move away from Log4J APIs.
